verses.text: And Elihu went on to say:
“Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’

xrefs.text: But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.
though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?
then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.
For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?

verses.text: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’

xrefs.text: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
You have said, ‘It is futile to serve God. What have we gained by keeping His requirements and walking mournfully before the LORD of Hosts?
If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’
Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.

verses.text: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.

xrefs.text: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.

verses.text: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.

xrefs.text: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts.
He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth; its dwellers are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.
And the LORD took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”

verses.text: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?

xrefs.text: But am I the One they are provoking? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves they spite, to their own shame?
But he who fails to find me harms himself; all who hate me love death.”
If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage; but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences.

verses.text: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?

xrefs.text: I said to the LORD, “You are my Lord; apart from You I have no good thing.”
“Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.
“Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”
If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage; but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences.

verses.text: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.

xrefs.text: Was not Achan son of Zerah unfaithful regarding what was set apart for destruction, bringing wrath upon the whole congregation of Israel? Yet it was not only Achan who perished because of his sin!’”
and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.
So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe that destroyed the cities where he had lived.
But Phinehas stood and intervened, and the plague was restrained.
What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?

verses.text: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.

xrefs.text: After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.
They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
“For the cause of the oppressed and for the groaning of the needy, I will now arise,” says the LORD. “I will bring safety to him who yearns.”
And now the cry of the Israelites has reached Me, and I have seen how severely the Egyptians are oppressing them.

For the choirmaster. To the tune of “A Dove on Distant Oaks.” A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Be merciful to me, O God, for men are hounding me; all day they press their attack.

verses.text: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,

xrefs.text: The LORD decrees His loving devotion by day, and at night His song is with me as a prayer to the God of my life.
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
Let the saints exult in glory; let them shout for joy upon their beds.
At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered:

But you have forgotten the LORD, your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in terror all day long because of the fury of the oppressor who is bent on destruction. But where is the fury of the oppressor?

verses.text: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’

xrefs.text: Blessed is the man You discipline, O LORD, and teach from Your law,
Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.

Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”

verses.text: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.

xrefs.text: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.
Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
Have mercy on us, O LORD, have mercy, for we have endured much contempt.
Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”

verses.text: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.

xrefs.text: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘I am about to bring upon them a disaster that they cannot escape. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen to them.
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.
The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.

verses.text: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,

xrefs.text: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it.
Clouds and darkness surround Him; righteousness and justice are His throne’s foundation.
Rest in God alone, O my soul, for my hope comes from Him.
Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.

verses.text: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!

xrefs.text: I will attend to their transgression with the rod, and to their iniquity with stripes.

How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.

verses.text: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”

xrefs.text: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard these very words:
‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.
